a crash course in good and bad controls: embedding edition

using embeddings to adjust for confounding is complicated

Author

Alex Hayes

Published

August 16, 2026

“representation learning”

  1. how should we use fancy machine learning models – one idea, broadly construed, is to take various “non-euclidean” kinds of data (read: anything that isn’t a number in a csv), embed it using some foundation model or something along those lines. lots of people are doing this; doing it well is clearly important and smart

  2. in this literature, the framing is always that we are learning a representation of confounders; that is, things that we need to adjust for to get valid causal estimates. but what should we actually adjust for Cinelli et al. (2022):

  • TODO

what should not adjust for:

  • mediators
  • colliders
  • post-outcome variables
  • post-treatment variables
Code 
library(ggdag)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)

node_colors <- c(
  exposure = "grey30",
  outcome  = "grey30",
  bad      = "#B2182B",
  latent   = "grey70"
)

plot_bad_control <- function(dag_data, title, subtitle) {
  ggplot(dag_data, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend)) +
    geom_dag_edges(edge_color = "grey50") +
    geom_dag_point(aes(color = role), size = 16) +
    geom_dag_text(color = "white", size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
    scale_color_manual(values = node_colors, guide = "none") +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_dag() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5, color = "grey30")
    )
}

# mediator: X -> M -> Y, X -> Y
mediator <- dagify(
  Y ~ X + M,
  M ~ X,
  exposure = "X",
  outcome = "Y",
  coords = list(x = c(X = 0, M = 1, Y = 2), y = c(X = 0, M = 1, Y = 0))
) |>
  tidy_dagitty()
mediator$data$role <- ifelse(mediator$data$name == "M", "bad", "outcome")

# collider: X -> C <- Y, X -> Y
collider <- dagify(
  Y ~ X,
  C ~ X + Y,
  exposure = "X",
  outcome = "Y",
  coords = list(x = c(X = 0, C = 1, Y = 2), y = c(X = 0, C = 1, Y = 0))
) |>
  tidy_dagitty()
collider$data$role <- ifelse(collider$data$name == "C", "bad", "outcome")

# post-treatment variable: X -> Z <- U -> Y, X -> Y, U unmeasured
post_treatment <- dagify(
  Y ~ X + U,
  Z ~ X + U,
  exposure = "X",
  outcome = "Y",
  latent = "U",
  coords = list(x = c(X = 0, Z = 1, U = 1, Y = 2), y = c(X = 0, Z = 1, U = 2, Y = 0))
) |>
  tidy_dagitty()
post_treatment$data$role <- dplyr::case_when(
  post_treatment$data$name == "Z" ~ "bad",
  post_treatment$data$name == "U" ~ "latent",
  TRUE ~ "outcome"
)

# post-outcome variable: X -> Y -> P
post_outcome <- dagify(
  Y ~ X,
  P ~ Y,
  exposure = "X",
  outcome = "Y",
  coords = list(x = c(X = 0, Y = 1, P = 2), y = c(X = 0, Y = 0, P = 0))
) |>
  tidy_dagitty()
post_outcome$data$role <- ifelse(post_outcome$data$name == "P", "bad", "outcome")

p1 <- plot_bad_control(mediator$data, "mediator", "blocks part of the X → Y effect")
p2 <- plot_bad_control(collider$data, "collider", "opens a spurious path between X and Y")
p3 <- plot_bad_control(post_treatment$data, "post-treatment variable", "amplifies bias from unmeasured U")
p4 <- plot_bad_control(post_outcome$data, "post-outcome variable", "hasn't happened yet when X acts")

(p1 | p2) / (p3 | p4)

  1. okay, so we have some image/network/text, we estimate some embeddings, and then we go forth and adjust for it. when can this go wrong: whenever the latent features in the embeddings are mediators, colliders, etc, etc

  2. how can you know if the latent features you learned in the embedding are mediators, colliders, etc. in general you can’t tell just from the embedding, since it only captures statistical dependence, not causal role. you need something from outside the data, like a plausible DAG, timing info, or an intervention, to sort that out.

References

Cinelli, Carlos, Andrew Forney, and Judea Pearl. 2022. “A Crash Course in Good and Bad Controls.” Sociological Methods & Research, 1–34. https://doi.org/10.1177/00491241221099552.
